lines.text: Morning, come through and take a seat. What can I help with?
I'm coming in with low back pain that shoots into my right buttock.
And how long has that been going on for?
About a fortnight now, ever since I lifted a bag of compost.
Any numbness in the saddle area, or changes going to the toilet?
No, going to the toilet is all normal, and I haven't had any numbness.
There's a bit of tingling down the back of my right thigh at night, though whether it's every night I really couldn't say, my partner reckons I kick about in my sleep anyway.
Okay. Let me have a look at how you move. Bend forwards for me as far as is comfortable.
Your fingertips stop just above your knees and the pain comes on near the end.
Lie back for me and I'll lift the right leg. Tell me when you feel it.
There, that pulls right down the back.
That's at about forty degrees, and the left side goes much higher without any bother.
I suspect this is probably an irritated nerve root rather than anything sinister, but I'd want to see how it settles.
For now, keep moving little and often, walk for ten minutes every couple of hours and avoid sitting for longer than half an hour.
If you lose feeling between your legs or can't control your bladder, ring 999 or go straight to A and E.
Right, will do. Thanks ever so much.
You're welcome. Take care of yourself, and mind that compost.
